newsitem.title: CHINA: China movie audiences slump on competition, cost.
newsitem.headline: China movie audiences slump on competition, cost.

text.p: China's movie audiences have slumped in the last decade, hit by competition from television and video as well as by the soaring cost of tickets, the Market Daily said on Monday.
China's cinemas sold tickets to eight billion theatre-goers in 1996, compared with sales of 29.3 billion in 1984, the newspaper said.
It attributed the slump to new forms of recreation such as television, videos and video compact discs.
In addition, cinema ticket prices have skyrocketed, soaring in Beijing to 20 yuan ($2.4) in 1996 from 0.2 yuan in 1984, it said.

Some cinemas in larger cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, and southern Guangzhou, have cut ticket prices for certain shows to a more acceptable level of 2-3 yuan in the last few months, and as a result, audiences have soared more than 10 times, the newspaper said.
